name: grpc_homa (Homa transport plugin for gRPC)
workload: gRPC round-trip time for short unary RPCs using an insecure channel, comparing the stock TCP transport against the Homa transport plugin (HomaClient/HomaListener)
claimed_speedup: short RPCs complete about 40% faster with Homa than with TCP (about 55 us round trip for Homa, vs. 90 us for TCP)
tradeoffs: Requires the PlatformLab/HomaModule Linux kernel module installed on every machine; only insecure gRPC channels are supported; C++ support is functional but Java support is only partially implemented; author states the project is no longer under active development.
caveats: The 55us-vs-90us figure is stated in the README with no disclosed hardware, CPU model, compiler flags, or methodology ('Initial performance measurements'), so it is a first-party rough claim, not a reproducible benchmark. No LICENSE file is present in the repo.
found_via: GitHub: gh repo list PlatformLab (surfaced after `gh search repos "Homa transport"` found PlatformLab/HomaModule, whose README links to grpc_homa as 'Preliminary support for using Homa with gRPC')

name: Homa (HomaModule) — Linux kernel implementation of the Homa RPC transport protocol
workload: 40-node CloudLab cluster; basic back-to-back single-client RPC latency/throughput (Table 2) plus four of the 'Montazeri' request/response workloads under high network load, measuring P50/P99/P999 tail latency across message sizes; Homa is explicitly designed as a transport for datacenter RPC frameworks (paper names gRPC and Apache Thrift as the frameworks it targets)
claimed_speedup: P99 tail latency 7-83x lower than TCP and DCTCP across all message sizes under high load; basic 100-byte RPC latency 15.1us (Homa) vs 23.4us (TCP) vs 24.1us (DCTCP); client RPC rate 1.6 Mops/sec (Homa) vs 1.0 Mops/sec (TCP)
compiler_and_flags: Linux kernel module built against Linux 5.4.80 via the repo's standard kernel Makefile; no userspace optimization flags reported (kernel-module benchmark, not a userspace std-facility comparison)
hardware: CloudLab xl170 nodes: Intel Xeon E5-2640v4 (10 cores, 2.4GHz), 4x16GB DDR4-2400, Intel DC S3520 480GB SSD, Mellanox ConnectX-4 25Gbps NIC, Mellanox 2410 switch, 40-node cluster
tradeoffs: Requires a custom Linux kernel module (no macOS/Windows, no unprivileged/userspace-only path); new homa_send/homa_recv/homa_reply socket API is not backward-compatible with existing TCP/UDP socket code, so gRPC/Thrift apps need a shim (see grpc_homa) to use it transparently; needs specific NIC support (Mellanox ConnectX-4/5/6, Intel E810 verified); paper states small-message throughput is still 5-10x below raw NIC line rate due to software/kernel overhead.
caveats: The headline 7-83x win is for tail latency of short messages under contention/high load, not raw bandwidth: the paper's own Table 2 shows a single-connection 500KB throughput test where Homa (10.0 Gbps) is actually LOWER than TCP (20.3 Gbps). Baseline compared directly is TCP/DCTCP, not gRPC or Thrift themselves; the RPC-framework connection is via the separate, less mature PlatformLab/grpc_homa shim (reported as a companion entry).
found_via: GitHub: gh search repos "Homa transport" -> PlatformLab/HomaModule; paper linked from repo README (USENIX ATC 2021, https://www.usenix.org/system/files/atc21-ousterhout.pdf)
